scholarships.title: Aotearoa New Zealand Tāwhia te Mana Research Fellowships — New Zealand Mana Tūāpapa Future Leader Fellowship

existing.description: The Mana Tūāpapa Future Leader Fellowship is the early-career scheme within the Aotearoa New Zealand Tāwhia te Mana Research Fellowships, administered by Royal Society Te Apārangi on behalf of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment. It funds employed researchers within 0-4 years of research experience after PhD conferral to build the foundations of an independent research career. Around 20 fellowships are awarded each year, each worth NZ$820,000 over four years, made up of salary contribution, institutional overheads and research expenses. The scheme replaced the previous Rutherford Discovery, Rutherford Foundation and James Cook Research Fellowships.
eligibility: Within 0-4 years of research experience after PhD conferral
Based at a New Zealand host research organisation registered in the on-line application system
May make only one Tāwhia te Mana Fellowship application per funding round
A former successful applicant may not apply for a second Fellowship in the same scheme
A previous holder of a Rutherford Discovery Fellowship or the James Cook Research Fellowship may not apply for an equivalent Tāwhia te Mana Fellowship
Not eligible if the applicant has previously received substantial research grant funding in a leadership capacity, such as principal investigator on a Marsden Fast Start or Endeavour grant
existing.eligibility_summary: Researchers within 0-4 years of research experience after PhD conferral, hosted by a registered New Zealand research organisation. Applicants must not previously have held a Tāwhia te Mana Fellowship in the same scheme or an equivalent Rutherford Discovery / James Cook Research Fellowship, and must not have held substantial research grant funding in a leadership capacity such as principal investigator on a Marsden Fast Start or Endeavour grant.
benefits: NZ$820,000 total value over four years
NZ$82,500 per year institutional overheads to the host organisation
Participation in the hui-a-tau annual workshop providing multi-disciplinary and multi-institutional links across the science, innovation and technology system
Leadership development and extension of the fellow's leadership role within their host organisation
coverage: Salary contribution of NZ$82,500 per year
Institutional overheads of NZ$82,500 per year
Research expenses of NZ$40,000 per year
requirements: Register as a prospective host in the on-line web-based application system (portal) — registration opens at any time
Submit the proposal in the portal before it closes at 2.00pm NZST on the published closing date
Nominate referees who will be invited by Royal Society Te Apārangi after the closing date (invitations issued by 15 July 2026 for the 2026 round)
Ballot applications and forward them to the selection panel
documents: Research proposal submitted through the on-line web-based application system
Application templates (provided by the Society; portal access is arranged via the host organisation's research office)
Referee reports solicited by the applicant
application_method: Proposal guidelines and application templates are published by the Society
Portal access is obtained by contacting the host organisation's research office
existing.selection_notes: Selection is determined by the Ministry in conjunction with Royal Society Te Apārangi. For the 2026 round: panellist scores due 11 September 2026, Final Review Panel Meeting early October 2026, results announced late October 2026. The Society notes the process 'will reflect MBIE's Diversity in Science Statement, with a commitment to ensure equity, diversity and inclusion in the final cohort of funded Fellows'.
existing.best_fit: New Zealand-based researchers 0-4 years post-PhD who hold an academic or research appointment and need salary, overhead and research funding to establish independence.
existing.notes: Government funded by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE); Royal Society Te Apārangi was selected through an open tender to administer the Fellowships. Budget 2023 allocated $44.38 million over four years in new funding for fellowships for emerging talent.
existing.application_period: Annual funding round. 2026 round: 1 May 2026 to 2.00pm NZST, 9 July 2026; results announced late October 2026. Next round dates not yet published.
existing.deadline_display: For the 2026 round the on-line portal opened Friday 1 May 2026 and closed at 2.00pm NZST on Thursday 9 July 2026; the Society has not published the opening or closing dates for the next round.

scholarships.title: Ngarimu VC and 28th (Māori) Battalion Memorial Scholarships
scholarships.official_source: Ngarimu VC and 28th (Māori) Battalion Memorial Scholarship Fund Board — Ministry of Education

existing.description: The Ngarimu VC and 28th (Māori) Battalion Memorial Scholarships are annual awards funded by the Ngarimu VC and 28th (Māori) Battalion Memorial Scholarship Fund Board, established in 1945, and administered through the Ministry of Education. They are awarded to exceptional Māori students for vocational or tertiary study who demonstrate values aligned with those of the 28th (Māori) Battalion. Following a $100,000 per year increase from the 2026-27 Budget, 14 scholarships are awarded each year across five schemes: 5 VET, 4 undergraduate, 3 master's, 1 Master of Education research and 1 doctoral. Applicants must be of Māori descent or whakapapa to a recognised Māori iwi and be enrolling in or continuing full-time tertiary study.
eligibility: Of Māori descent or whakapapa to a recognised Māori iwi
Enrolling in, or already enrolled to continue, full-time tertiary study for the academic year the scholarship supports
VET applicants: course leads to a certificate or diploma at NZQA levels 4 to 7, at least 120 credits total, studied full time
VET applicants are not eligible if they are doing a bachelor's degree — they apply for the Ngarimu undergraduate scholarship instead
VET level 4 apprenticeships are eligible if the applicant has completed years 1 to 2 and is enrolling in their third or fourth subsequent year
Preference will be given to applicants whose studies aim to improve the social, economic and cultural wellbeing of Māori
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be of Māori descent or whakapapa to a recognised Māori iwi, and must be enrolling in or already enrolled to continue full-time tertiary study for the relevant academic year. The selection panel gives preference to applicants whose studies aim to improve the social, economic and cultural wellbeing of Māori. VET applicants need a certificate or diploma at NZQA levels 4 to 7 (minimum 120 credits, full time) and cannot be studying a bachelor's degree.
benefits: 4 undergraduate scholarships of up to $30,000 each
3 master's scholarships of up to $20,000 each
1 Master of Education research scholarship of up to $20,000
Support to 'build knowledge, develop as leaders and give back to their whānau, hapū, iwi and communities'
coverage: VET scholarships: $10,000 each for study of a minimum of 120 credits at NZQA level 4 to 7 non-degree
Undergraduate scholarships: up to $30,000 each ($10,000 per year of full-time study for up to 3 years)
Master's scholarships: up to $20,000 each ($10,000 per year of full-time study for up to 2 years)
Master of Education research scholarship: up to $20,000 ($10,000 per year of full-time study for up to 2 years)
Doctoral scholarship: up to $40,000 ($20,000 per year of full-time study for up to 2 years)
requirements: Submit the online application form on the Ministry of Education page when applications are open
Be enrolled in the course in the year the scholarship money is paid — the Ministry states 'if you apply for the scholarship in 2026, you will get the money for the scholarship in 2027'
Read the Ngarimu scholarships application guidance published by the Ministry
documents: Record of achievement or other record of learning (verified tertiary academic transcript, MyBCITO record, NZQA record of achievement, or provider record) — for undergraduate applicants who have not yet started study, an NZQA record of learning for NCEA Level 2 (and Level 3 if applicable) or equivalent Cambridge International Examinations or International Baccalaureate

Reference or endorsement commenting on academic achievement and suitability to study or training, from someone involved in the applicant's study or training journey — it cannot be from a friend or family member
For master's and Master of Education research applicants: a brief statement of up to 250 words on the topic, reasons for interest in the subject area and future expectations
For doctoral applicants: a 500-word essay on the thesis/doctorate topic and future expectations
For doctoral applicants: a reference from the chief supervisor commenting on academic abilities and commitment, and confirming acceptance into the PhD programme
application_method: Online application form published on the Ministry of Education Ngarimu scholarships page
Applications are open for a fixed window each year
existing.selection_notes: A selection panel assesses applications. The Ministry states it will 'give preference to applicants who demonstrate that their studies aim to improve the social, economic and cultural wellbeing of Māori'. Outcomes for the 2027 study year are expected to be notified to all applicants by late November 2026.
existing.best_fit: Māori students entering or continuing full-time vocational, undergraduate, master's or doctoral study in New Zealand who can evidence achievement and alignment with the values of the 28th (Māori) Battalion.
existing.notes: The Fund Board was established in 1945 by the Ngarimu VC and 28th (Māori) Battalion Memorial Scholarship Fund Act 1945 and exists to promote the study and maintenance of te reo Māori, Māori history, Māori tradition and Māori culture. The 2026-27 Budget increased Fund funding by $100,000 each year, adding 5 scholarships and bringing the annual total to 14. Winners for the 2025/26 round were announced on 26 March 2026 at a ceremony at Parliament, Te Whanganui-a-Tara.
existing.duration: Up to 3 years (undergraduate); up to 2 years (master's); up to 2 years (doctoral)
existing.application_period: Annual. 2027 study year: applications closed Sunday 19 July 2026, outcomes notified by late November 2026. 2028 study year: applications open mid-2027.
existing.deadline_display: Applications to support study in 2027 closed on Sunday 19 July 2026, and the Ministry expects to notify all applicants of outcomes by late November 2026. Applications to support study in 2028 will open mid-2027; no exact 2028 closing date is published.
